title: Art
author: rgs2007
selftext:
I can generate the code and the mechanics with AI but the art and sprites (movement) looks terrible. 

Any tips?

I'm a software developer but not game developer.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: Pixel art or other? I’m using pixel lab as a plugin in aseprite.

comments.author: PushDeep9980
comments.body: Work with it to make concept art. Get some references, then ask it to make sprites/pixel art out of your references. Feed it reference video of other inspiration of sprites you like so it can see what movement looks like. Try different chats. Try hooking up a blender mcp server and have it make your stuff in blender. Idk just try stuff.

comments.author: Suecotero
comments.body:
ChatGPT does decent sprites if you prompt it properly, i.e.

>A sprite sheet of painted dust and smoke puffs for a video game visual effect: the dust cloud a rocket kicks up as it lands on dry, rocky ground.   
  
Layout: a 4 x 4 grid of 16 separate puffs on a 2048 x 2048 square image, one puff per 512 x 512 cell, each centred in its cell with clear empty margin around it, never touching the cell edges or each other. No grid lines, no labels, no text.  
  
Background: solid pure black (#000000) everywhere outside the puffs, with no gradient, vignette, ground, horizon or shadow.  
  
The puffs:  
  
 Rows 1 to 3: twelve round, billowing dust clouds, each a cluster of soft overlapping lobes like cauliflower-shaped rocket exhaust dust. Vary them: some dense and compact, some loose and wispy, some with a bright dense core fading to thin ragged edges, a few elongated or lopsided. Sizes range from filling most of the cell to about half of it.  
  
\- Row 4: four low, wide, flattened ground-hugging dust sheets, like dust blasted sideways along the ground, much wider than tall, with rolling curled leading edges and thin trailing wisps.  
  
Colour and light: neutral, nearly colourless light grey to off-white dust (it will be tinted in the game to match each planet's soil). Soft, diffuse light from above, so each puff is a little brighter on top and slightly darker underneath, with gentle internal shading that shows the volume of the lobes. Matte, opaque and dusty, like fine regolith rather than steam or white cloud. No fire, no glow, no sparks, no hard outlines, no visible brush strokes.  
  
Edges: soft, feathered edges that fade smoothly into the black, so the brightness of each pixel can be used as its transparency.  
  
Style: realistic, painterly but clean, readable at small size, like high-quality smoke sprites for a real-time game. Seen from slightly above.

comments.author: Coolmacde
comments.body: I use chat gpt to make png files with transparent backgrounds.  Tell gpt you want to use the image you uploaded and make 8 cycles of whatever movement you want like walking, punching etc.

comments.author: RoutineDoctor4151
comments.body: This is so true, bro. Almost every programmer who transitions to independent development gets stuck at this hurdle—the infamous "Programmer Art" disaster. The code runs, the physics are perfect, but when the characters move, it looks like a ridiculous PowerPoint presentation, even exuding a strange sense of low quality.This is actually quite normal, because art and animation are completely different skill sets.

comments.author: the_builder_ai
comments.body:
GPT Astra / Sol 6.1 actually does a decent job of animating 2D art/sprites. My flow is to let it give you the character art. Do all the visual edits at this level. Once you are satisfied -> Tell it to make sprite sheets. Here, you will want to know what sort of actions/animations your character has. The usuals are like idle, walk, etc. Once you have that in mind, you can tell it to animate and ChatGPT can actually animate moving characters. There are errors sometimes but you just need to keep prompting and fixing.

Unfortunately Opus doesn't do well because it doesn't have image gen capabilities.
